exposure: maternal pre-pregnancy BMI (healthy weight, overweight, obese)
mode of delivery (Caesarean section vs vaginal)
outcome: newborn skin microbiome (relative abundance of bacterial genera)
newborn oral microbiome (relative abundance of bacterial genera)
cohort: The study included 39 newborns from 39 pregnant participants categorized by pre-pregnancy BMI into healthy weight, overweight, and obese groups.
finding: Newborns of obese participants had a higher relative abundance of Peptoniphilus in their skin microbiome, and neonates born via C-section had a higher relative abundance of Ureaplasma in their oral microbiome.
mod_finding: Neonates born via C-section had a higher relative abundance of Ureaplasma in their oral microbiome compared to neonates delivered vaginally.
